question.text: Mr. Sameer Joshi, Head of Fund Operations at Yamuna Cat I VC Fund (2019 vintage), is asked by an institutional LP: 'Where does your 18% Net IRR rank versus peer 2019-vintage India VC funds?' Per Section 10.8 and SEBI's benchmarking-agency framework, which approach is MOST appropriate for Cat I/II AIFs?

answer.text: Benchmark the fund against NIFTY 50 price return (no TRI) on a point-to-point basis across fund tenure.

Use vintage-year peer benchmarking — compare the fund's pooled IRR, TVPI, DPI, and RVPI against the database of 2019-vintage India Cat I AIFs maintained by an IVCA-appointed Benchmarking Agency (CRISIL, NSE, Preqin) under the SEBI framework.
Benchmark against a fixed hurdle rate such as 10% p.a. with no peer comparison, as vintage-year matching is not required under SEBI rules.
Use the Sensex 30 as the sole benchmark since Cat I funds predominantly invest in Indian equities.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 10.8 and 10.8.1, vintage-year peer benchmarks for Cat I/II AIFs are built using pooled IRR, investment multiples, DPI, RVPI, and TVPI. The benchmarking agencies are appointed via IVCA under the SEBI framework — CRISIL, NSE, and Preqin. The Trap: Option A uses a point-to-point equity return that is cash-flow blind. Option C describes the Cat III absolute-return approach — not Cat I/II. Option D applies a broad-based equity index to early-stage illiquid investments. Note: Reporting is done on a half-yearly basis using comparable fund tenure with peer funds of the same vintage year.
